claim: Detects SQLite databases with write-ahead log (WAL) or shared-memory (SHM) sidecars and blocks raw copy
where: landing workflow, CLI scan and guard, README
sandbox: fresh temporary folder created by dbsync-safe --demo

claim: Creates a checksummed SQLite snapshot at the chosen output path without changing any source path or file byte
sandbox: closed WAL-mode database; compare the recursive source tree, modes, sizes, and SHA-256 values before and after snapshot

claim: Snapshots and restores a closed SQLite database with a finalized persistent rollback journal without changing its source
sandbox: fresh closed journal_mode=PERSIST database with its finalized journal; compare the exact source tree and query the restored row

claim: Snapshots a read-only SQLite source without changing any source path or file byte
sandbox: closed WAL-mode database in a 0555 directory with a 0444 main file; run as uid/gid 65534 when root; compare the exact tree

claim: SQLite opens only private working and output copies during snapshot acquisition
sandbox: Linux syscall interposer records open flags during closed-WAL, active-WAL, and persistent-journal snapshots; source paths must be read-only and a private acquisition path read-write

claim: Restores a packet into another folder after checksum and SQLite integrity checks
sandbox: fresh dbsync-safe --demo packet and restore folder

claim: Refuses to replace an existing target database unless force is passed
sandbox: fresh packet and target containing sentinel bytes; require refusal and byte-identical target

claim: The bundled demo restores all 4 sample notes, including the note written to the live WAL
sandbox: fresh CLI demo; query its restored sample and compare the observed count and live-WAL note with the browser result

claim: Every CLI command accepts machine-readable JSON, including both demo spellings
sandbox: fresh source, packet, target, and missing paths; parse success and error output from scan, guard, snapshot, verify, restore, demo, and --demo

claim: The CLI demo creates and uses only bundled sample files in its process-specific local temporary folder
where: landing demo, CLI demo output, README
sandbox: run the bundled CLI demo and assert all generated sample, packet, and restored paths remain within its local temporary root

claim: The CLI needs no account or credentials
sandbox: inspect production CLI help and command surface for any sign-in, credential, token, account, or API-key workflow

claim: The CLI sends no network requests
sandbox: run scan, guard, snapshot, verify, restore, demo, and --demo with an LD_PRELOAD interposer that records and denies all IPv4/IPv6 sockets

claim: The CLI has no telemetry and the web demo saves nothing
where: landing facts, demo banner, privacy, README
sandbox: fresh browser context on /demo records every request and storage key; locked Rust graph is checked for HTTP clients

claim: The landing page requests public release details only from GitHub and caches them for one hour
sandbox: fresh browser context with a recorded GitHub API response; assert exact outbound origin, expiry, cache reuse, and refresh

claim: The tool handles SQLite files and ignores other file formats
sandbox: fresh folder containing .db and text files without SQLite headers; assert no databases are reported

claim: Free under the MIT License
sandbox: fresh clone; inspect the shipped LICENSE

claim: The shell installer rejects a SHA-256 mismatch before installing
sandbox: temporary install directory, local release archive, and deliberately incorrect published digest

sandbox: GitHub Releases API for the public latest release; assert all ten assets and parse latest.json with eight package URLs

claim: The repository includes versioned Homebrew, Scoop, and winget package manifests
sandbox: fresh clone; parse or inspect all three manifests and match version, release URL, and SHA-256 shape

sandbox: fresh clone after npm ci; run the exact Rust scenario test and npm run build, then assert target/release/dbsync-safe and dist/site/index.html
